knowledge_base: Subprocess isolation with resource.setrlimit caps memory on POSIX; Windows requires Job Objects via pywin32.
Wall-clock timeout is enforced by SIGKILL after a grace SIGTERM; record both so the caller knows which fired.
Stdout and stderr should be captured separately; merging them hides which stream a traceback came from.
Sys.path should be reset to a known prefix so user code cannot import modules from the caller's working directory.
Builtin import is restricted by an audit hook (PEP 578) that rejects modules outside the allowlist before loading.
ResourceWarning at exit is normal for short scripts that open files; suppress it from stderr to reduce noise.
Faulthandler should be enabled so segfaults in C extensions still produce a traceback in stderr.
On Linux, prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS) plus a minimal seccomp filter blocks syscalls like socket and execve.
Working directory is a fresh tempdir per run; never reuse the same dir because user code can leave state.
Exit codes follow shell convention: 0 ok, 1 generic error, 124 timeout, 137 OOM-killed (128+9).

templates.timeout: TimeoutError after {timeout_s}s; sent SIGTERM then SIGKILL.
templates.denied_import: ImportError: '{module}' is not on the allowlist.
